res: CH4 and CO2 in an H2-rich atmosphere, no NH3. Possible DMS/DMDS claims are tentative and disputed; hycean vs. mini-Neptune still debated.
CH4, CO2, H2O; metal-enriched atmosphere, consistent with a miscible envelope.
Hints of a N2-rich secondary atmosphere; not a firm detection. Candidate water world / temperate rocky planet.
High-metallicity atmosphere with reflective aerosols; muted spectral features.
Featureless; rules out metallicities below ~175x solar unless aerosols sit at <~1 mbar.
Featureless; high metallicity and/or high-altitude aerosols. Also gave precise transit timings (TTVs).
Evidence for CH4 (~1% mixing ratio) in an H2-rich atmosphere; no NH3 or HCN.
Strong CH4, moderate-to-strong CO2; no significant sulfur species. Consistent with a deep H2-rich atmosphere.

No molecular features detected in the 3-5 um spectrum; rules out metallicities below ~180-240x solar for cloud tops above 1 mbar. Planet may sit near the threshold where small-planet atmospheric features become detectable.
Water detected (consistent with solar metallicity); hints of SO2 and CO; no CO2 or CH4. Low mean molecular weight and no appreciable haze, unlike M-dwarf sub-Neptunes.
Compatible with a water-rich (steam) atmosphere; H2-dominated solutions disfavored.
Hints of sulfur-bearing volatiles (SO2/H2S), volatile-rich interior. At the super-Earth/sub-Neptune boundary.
Largely featureless, consistent with high mean molecular weight and/or aerosols.
